reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: While direct PD-L1 binding data is not provided, atezolizumab is a well-established anti-PD-L1 antibody with known target engagement. The dosing regimen (IV infusion every 3 weeks) is standard for this class. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: The mechanism predicts immune activation and anti-tumor response. Evidence of pathway modulation includes higher objective response rate (16.9% vs 7.9%) and longer duration of response (14.0 vs 7.8 months), suggesting immune system activation. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: The primary endpoint (OS) was met with HR 0.78 (95% CI 0.63-0.97, p=0.025), representing a 22% reduction in death risk. This is clinically meaningful for advanced NSCLC. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Interestingly, the PD-L1 positive subgroup showed numerically similar but non-significant benefit (HR 0.84, p=0.272), suggesting the mechanism may work broadly rather than just in biomarker-selected patients. 5. CONFOUNDERS: No major trial design issues identified. Lower AE rate vs comparator suggests good tolerability.

failure_modes.evidence: While overall trial succeeded, the PD-L1 positive subgroup (expected to be most responsive) showed non-significant benefit (p=0.272), suggesting complex population effects
